subject: List from packages.renjin that have passed all tests?

messages.author: 66f8e6ad58d88e82
messages.subject: List from packages.renjin that have passed all tests?
parts:
I am doing a survey of what R packages are available for renjin. This is in support of a project to develop Processing.R, a renjin-based R mode for the Processing language/IDE.

Is there a way to find a listing from packages.renjin.org of anything that "passed all tests"?

I have only found the search interface, and with so many packages from BioConductor and CRAN it has been very slow going trying to get a sense of what is available -- out of the first ten that I tried scattershot (graph, lubridate, pcaMethods, stringr, etc.),  I only found one with an affirmative listing (plyr).

messages.author: 3b104dc6686d0c85
messages.subject: Re: List from packages.renjin that have passed all tests?
parts:
Hi Jeremy,

I love Processing, therefore this sounds incredibly interesting. I have always felt that Renjin is a great match for Processing and I have put together a little example in the past to demonstrate how easy it is to load Renjin into a Processing sketch. I'd love to learn more about your ideas regarding this "R mode" for Processing, do you have any public project/information available to share?

We can query our build system to get you the information you are looking for. But be aware: passing all tests currently only means that none of the examples in a package result in an error. There are packages with little or no examples, or even just very trivial examples, therefore this is not a 100% guarantee that the package will work flawlessly in Renjin.

Regards,

Maarten-Jan Kallen

messages.author: 66f8e6ad58d88e82
messages.subject: Re: List from packages.renjin that have passed all tests?
parts:
Thank you so much, Maarten-Jan --

Please do query the build system for passing packages -- I would greatly appreciate it. I understand that test passing isn't a guarantee, but it would be a great first-pass to help begin a search.

Very glad to hear that you find the project interesting -- and thanks for sharing that example!

Processing.R is a Google Summer of Code 2017 project proposed by the very talented Ce Gao -- I am acting as his GSOC mentor on behalf of the Processing Foundation. Just as the "Processing.py" Python Mode uses Jython to enable Processing-in-Python, the "Processing.R" R Language Mode uses Renjin to enable coding Processing-in-R. Part of the early work is in mapping out calls to the Processing(Java) API -- e.g. `processing$line(x,y,x2,y2)` -- and later in using pre-processing to make the API automagically available as a top-level namespace. 

There is a working alpha-level R Language mode for the command line and the Processing Development Environment (PDE) available here:

https://github.com/gaocegege/Processing.R

At present the release is old, and the latest mode should instead be built and installed with ant from master. Sometime soon we should have the mode integrated with PDE's built-in Contributions Manager for casual testing. If you or other members of the Renjin community are interested then we will keep you in the loop -- feedback and ideas would be most welcome.

very best,
Jeremy

messages.subject: Re: List from packages.renjin that have passed all tests?
parts:
The Processing.R project is still hoping to run some tests on R packages that are fully compatible with renjin.

1. Is there a way to find a listing from packages.renjin.org of anything that "passed all tests" -- for example, by querying the build system?
2. If not, do renjin devs know of a short list of any R packages that might be expected to just work out-of-the-box when imported in renjin? Even 2-3 suggestions would be a helpful place to start.

Many thanks,
Jeremy

messages.author: 3b104dc6686d0c85
messages.subject: Re: List from packages.renjin that have passed all tests?
parts:
Hi Jeremy,

why don't you try http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/plyr which is a popular package and which depends on Rcpp. It should work close to 100%.

There are also a couple of packages for which we provide drop-in replacements such as digest, rjson, and xml2. These may not implement the full functionality of the original R packages (e.g. xml2 has only a small subset of functions), but do work. They tend to be mostly infrastructure packages whose GNU R versions interface with system libraries.

Given that Processing.org is primarily used to create visuals, you should probably look at packages which provide interesting statistical models. So the built-in stats package should be on your list (e.g. to sample from different types of random variables) as well.

Other (near) 100% compatibility packages based on a totally random look through our package browser:
  • http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/changepoint
  • http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/foreach
  • http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/GeneF
  • http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/uniftest
  • http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/orthopolynom
  • http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/magrittr
  • http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/rateratio.test
  • http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/regexr
  • http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/rlm
  • http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/optR
  • http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/outliers
Hope this helps!
​
Maarten
